fig-14.observation: One natural crystal cluster on a dark rectangular background. Tall rear-left/central prismatic crystal with pointed faceted termination; a shorter upright rear-right crystal with asymmetrical faceted cap; a left foreground upright crystal; a right foreground inclined elongated crystal; a broad low front-center faceted crystal with dark side face and partly overlapping cap; partially occluded smaller growths among these; many irregular small faceted fragments at the base, concentrated across the lower-left/center and around the right crystal foot. Faces, shadow and overlap distinguish several crystals; it is not one regular solid or merely an opaque perimeter.
fig-14.sitesEdgesGrid: No atomic sites, bonds, measured edges, grid rows/columns or printed dimensions. Facet boundaries are semantic object/appearance information, not a measured geometry contract.
fig-14.relationships: Main prisms rise from and overlap a shared irregular small-crystal base. Tall crystal is behind the low broad front crystal; right-leaning prism is in front of the shorter rear-right crystal. Dark and light faces convey faceting and occlusion, without establishing measured 3D angles.
fig-14.uncertainty: Tiny overlapping base fragments cannot be assigned a defensible exact crystal count from this scan; no count is invented.
